ap_computer_science_a-f01.title: GridStats: the row with the largest sum

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write the method bestRow, which returns the index of the row of grid with the largest sum of its elements. If more than one row has the largest sum, the method returns the smallest such row index. For example, if grid is { { 1, 2 }, { 5, 0 }, { 3, 2 } } the row sums are 3, 5 and 5, so bestRow returns 1. Complete the method bestRow.

rubric_rows.criterion: Iterates over every row with a loop bounded by grid.length
Iterates over every element of the current row with bounds based on grid[r].length (or an enhanced for)
Accesses elements with the row index first and the column index second
Accumulates the sum of the current row (and resets it for each row)
required_elements: int sum = 0 inside the row loop

rubric_rows.criterion: Keeps track of the largest row sum seen so far, initialized so negative sums work
required_elements: bestSum initialized to the first row or a very small value

rubric_rows.criterion: Compares the current row sum with the best using a strict comparison so ties keep the smaller index
Records the row index (not the sum) of the best row when a new best is found
common_errors: stores the sum as the index

rubric_rows.criterion: Returns the row index after all rows have been examined
The method compiles with correct 2D array syntax and return type int

ap_computer_science_a-f02.title: GridTools: transpose a 2D array

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write the method transpose, which returns a new two-dimensional array that is the transpose of grid: for every row r and column c, the element at row c and column r of the result equals the element at row r and column c of grid. The array grid must not be modified. For example, if grid is { { 1, 2, 3 }, { 4, 5, 6 } } the method returns { { 1, 4 }, { 2, 5 }, { 3, 6 } }. Complete the method transpose.

rubric_rows.criterion: Creates a new two-dimensional array whose number of rows equals the number of columns of grid and whose number of columns equals the number of rows of grid
Iterates over every row with a loop bounded by grid.length
Iterates over every element of each row with correct column bounds
Reads from grid with the row index first and the column index second
Assigns each element read from grid into the result with the indexes exchanged
Handles a one-row or one-column array correctly: the allocation and both loops stay within bounds
common_errors: index out of bounds when rows differ from columns

rubric_rows.criterion: Allocates storage for every row of the result so no row of the result is missing
required_elements: new int[rows][cols] or each row allocated
common_errors: a row of the result is null

rubric_rows.criterion: Leaves grid unchanged
Returns the new array after all elements are copied, with return type int[][]

self_check_tests.call: int[][] g = new int[][] { { 1 } }; int[][] t = GridTools.transpose(g); return Arrays.deepToString(t) + "|" + Arrays.deepToString(g);
int[][] g = new int[][] { { 1, 2, 3 } }; int[][] t = GridTools.transpose(g); return Arrays.deepToString(t) + "|" + Arrays.deepToString(g);
int[][] g = new int[][] { { 1 }, { 2 } }; int[][] t = GridTools.transpose(g); return Arrays.deepToString(t) + "|" + Arrays.deepToString(g);
int[][] g = new int[][] { { 1, 2 }, { 3, 4 } }; int[][] t = GridTools.transpose(g); return Arrays.deepToString(t) + "|" + Arrays.deepToString(g);
int[][] g = new int[][] { { 1, 2, 3 }, { 4, 5, 6 } }; int[][] t = GridTools.transpose(g); return Arrays.deepToString(t) + "|" + Arrays.deepToString(g);
int[][] g = new int[][] { { 1, 2 }, { 3, 4 }, { 5, 6 } }; int[][] t = GridTools.transpose(g); return Arrays.deepToString(t) + "|" + Arrays.deepToString(g);
int[][] g = new int[][] { { 1, 2, 3 }, { 4, 5, 6 }, { 7, 8, 9 } }; int[][] t = GridTools.transpose(g); return Arrays.deepToString(t) + "|" + Arrays.deepToString(g);
int[][] g = new int[][] { { 7, 8, 9, 0 } }; int[][] t = GridTools.transpose(g); return Arrays.deepToString(t) + "|" + Arrays.deepToString(g);
